items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: And then later on, Lionel Hampton joined the small group as a quartet

ctx.x: And then later on, Lionel Hampton joined the small group as a quartet and that continued with me until 1939, and I left to form a big band of my own.

That's right -- now that's where I tie in with you -- in 1936, I came to New York to the Cotton Club with Cab Calloway, and you were with Goodman, and you had a contract to do a record with Billie Holiday.

items.title: Lionel Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: No. Because Teddy Wilson played it in the left hand.

ctx.x: No, no. People [inaudible], because we all played good music. And Benny presented us in a professional way. We were a part of his organization, and it would be noticeable that we were soft. And the people liked that. Some of the ovations that we used to get, it was the sound.
I thought it was interesting that that quartet didn’t use a bass player a lot.
No. Because Teddy Wilson played it in the left hand.
